concerns: aux_weight 0.05 may be too low to influence shared embeddings meaningfully; the method card suggests 0.1-0.3, but at this weight the term is nearly negligible and still did not beat the parent.
Using BPR as the ranking objective is itself an untested change relative to the pointwise baseline; the failure could be due to BPR plus aux rather than aux alone.
The robustness gap on random exposure is large (primary 0.361 vs validation 0.582), indicating limited generalisation headroom.
The best epoch was 1 with early stopping, suggesting the model overfit or did not improve beyond the first epoch; this hints that the auxiliary head added no real learning signal.
critic_postflight.next_focus: Pivot to the next untested direction with higher likelihood: user-behaviour sequences (history_features, specifically DIN/SIM-style interest modelling). The starter kit rates this as a completely blank direction, and the official features contain no behavioural history, so adding temporally safe, within-user recent-item aggregates crossed with item features (e.g., author, video tag) could provide the missing user-item interaction signal that multi-task supervision failed to capture. Keep the BPR or switch to group_softmax, but focus on building leakage-safe sequential features from train-only prior interactions.
critic_postflight.rationale: The multi-task probe (click auxiliary head at weight 0.05 with BPR) achieved primary 0.5820, below the baseline 0.6016, so the hypothesis is not supported on the trusted validation split. GAUC (0.6408) is below the baseline's GAUC and nDCG@5 (0.5233) also fails to offset, giving a primary that is 1.96 points worse. The auxiliary supervision did not help the sparse ranking signal; the shared-embedding assumption appears not to pay off at this weight. The negative result aligns with the method card's known failure mode where auxiliary gradients can drag embeddings toward the click objective without improving long_view ranking.

concerns: aux_weight=0.05 is the lower bound of the method-card safe range (0.05–0.3); if GAUC/nDCG improve, a follow-up at 0.1–0.3 may be justified.

critic_preflight.next_focus: If the click-aux BPR probe improves upon its parent, escalate aux_weight within the safe range and consider combining multi_task with the best history_features configuration; otherwise pivot back to history_features refinement (per-tab recency, video-age interaction).
critic_preflight.rationale: The proposal adds a low-weighted (aux_weight=0.05) click auxiliary head over the same shared FM embeddings to a BPR ranking objective. This is fully consistent with the multi_task method card's safe initial search space (click-only, aux_weight 0.05–0.3). Auxiliary targets come exclusively from build_aux_labels on train rows (train-only by construction, raising for any other split), so there is no leakage or hidden-test access. No cross-user negatives, no evaluator/split/label/budget changes, no unsafe imports or operations, and the candidate contract (FMRanker, build_features, CandidateOutput) is respected. Numerically it is a small additive loss term with no stability risk. Although the parent BPR run scored low (primary 0.555), this is a cheap, focused probe following a registered untested direction and does not warrant hard rejection.
